prompt: Match each decision to what it means.

pairs.right: build something so it is less likely or less harmful
live with it, on the record

prompt: Vereda stops sending the CPF to the gateway. Which decision is that, for the linking threat?

choices.text: Mitigate, because a control was added to the charge
choices.why: Nothing was added; something was removed.

choices.text: Eliminate
choices.why: Right: the data that made linking possible is gone.

choices.text: Transfer, because the gateway now carries the risk
choices.why: The gateway no longer receives it at all.

choices.text: Accept, because the CPF was never needed
choices.why: Accepting means living with it.

prompt: "Use a WAF" is proposed with no threat beside it. What does the lesson conclude?

choices.text: It is a good requirement as written, ready for the backlog
choices.why: It names a product, not a behaviour.

choices.text: It should be accepted as a risk until somebody can explain it
choices.why: It is a control, not a risk.

choices.text: It needs a CWE number first
choices.why: The missing piece is the threat.

choices.text: It answers an unwritten threat, or nothing
choices.why: Right: either write the threat down, or drop the control.

prompt: Why does T01 need two requirements?

choices.text: Because every threat must have two

choices.text: Because R01 is not testable
choices.why: It has a test.

choices.text: Because T01 is two threats
choices.why: It is one threat with two defences.
